newsitem.title: UK: UK transport group slams govt's bus deregulation.
newsitem.headline: UK transport group slams govt's bus deregulation.

text.p: The UK government faced a barrage of criticism over its flagship transport policy of bus deregulation on Wednesday in a report published by its own group of advisers.

The UK Round Table on Sustainable Development, a transport working group set up five years ago to address environmental issues by liaising with the government, said in its report "Making Connections" that bus deregulation and rail privatisation had produced a "fragmented" service which had no clear lines of responsibility to the consumer.

The statement issued by the gorup, which includes academics, businessmen and pressure groups including Transport 2000, said "For passenger transport, there are tensions between competition which can increase efficiency on specific routes and integration which is vital for journeys involving transfers.

"Over recent years deregulation of the bus industry and rail privatisation, together with reductions in local authority powers, have produced a more fragmented service and a lack of clear responsibility for ensuring the network benefits occur."
The group concluded that unless these issues were tackled the benefits of competition would be outweighed by its problems.
Dr Susan Owens, head of one of the sub-working groups, said issues like connections and transferable tickets were key to providing the consumer with an adequate service level.
She added that businesses considering sending freight by rail and road, rather than road alone, "face equivalent worries: the journey may take longer, cost more and be less reliable."
The Round Table's 30-strong group is co-chaired by the environment minister John Gummer.
